description: Fighter plan generation. How Fight IQ and Tactical Execution turn strategy and memory into a committed 8-slot plan. Values are initial candidates, not balanced.

pipeline.note: All randomness lives before commit. Once committed, resolution is fully deterministic per docs/design/26_action_result_resolution.md.

fight_iq.note: Fight IQ buys prediction quality and search breadth, never hidden information.
fight_iq.note_overfit: Low Fight IQ weights the single most recent turn far too heavily instead of reading across the memory window.

tactical_execution.note: Fidelity of the chosen plan. Applied as plan-stage perturbation, never as a resolution roll.

evaluation.note: pattern_repetition_penalty makes a fighter vary on its own. Without it, a strong evaluation converges on one optimal loop and becomes trivially readable.

survival_override.note: Condition-driven, not a separate personality. Any fighter falls back to recovery when the state demands it.

npc_information_cards.note: NPC info cards never read the current turn. The opponent commits after the NPC, so reading it would be circular and would look like cheating. They sharpen observation of PAST turns instead.

determinism.note: Same seed and same pre-turn state must produce the same committed plan. The plan is generated before any reveal and is never regenerated.
